text:
noah_cli: Heads up - installed redwoodctl on my laptop (macOS 12) and ran into a weird auth loop when doing local testing. redwoodctl version shows 0.14.0.

tara_installer: What flow are you using? browser callback or device code?

noah_cli: Browser callback. It opens the browser, I sign in, redirects to http://127.0.0.1:55678/callback but redwoodctl prints "received callback, validating... failed" then immediately starts auth again.

ben_sre: Sounds like the local listener is getting the callback but token exchange failing. Any proxy env vars (HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY) set? Those can make the outbound token request go via proxy and be blocked.

noah_cli: I do have HTTP_PROXY set for corp pypi. Unset it and retried - same behavior.

tara_installer: Could be an OpenSSL CA bundle mismatch in our bundled binary on macOS12. We saw intermittent TLS errors that result in 400/401 during token exchange and we retry the flow. What's in ~/.redwood/logs/last.log?

noah_cli: Log shows: "token exchange error: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority"

ben_sre: Yep. Temporary workaround: install certs via 'brew install ca-certificates' and set SSL_CERT_FILE env var to the bundle path, or use device flow: 'redwoodctl login --device'. We'll push a fix.

build-bot: ci: patched build to include updated cert bundle for macOS 12 - candidate 0.14.1-canary published.

noah_cli: Device flow worked fine. Thanks. Leaving a note that browser flow fails on older macOS due to bundled certs.

tara_installer: Action: backport cert bundle update to stable and add note to install guide about device-code fallback for corp/proxy/old-macos.

noah_cli: Filed DX ticket with logs: DX-700.

ben_sre: Also adding a quick diagnostic to redwoodctl that prints the TLS error and suggests device-code when cert check fails.

noah_cli: Perfect. Appreciated :thumbsup:
